static_traits.name: Li Jing
static_traits.educational_background: Currently studying for a bachelor's degree, majoring in business administration
static_traits.family_status: Father is a dentist,Mother is a Teacher
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive partner and close friends to confide in, but they may not fully understand the career-related Anxiety; partner relationship somewhat tense from stress and uncertainty
static_traits.medical_history: no history of similar psychological problems, no psychotherapy history; no significant physical illness history
static_traits.language_features: clear expression, fairly strong logic, able to identify and describe negative Automatic thoughts; highly cooperative, willing to try Homework; tone carrying Anxiety,Self-doubt; thinking with 'must/should'-style rule-based expressions

basic_info.main_problem: I believe working at a daycare will hinder me from getting Work related to my business administration major, which makes me feel uncertain and afraid about career prospects. This feeling appeared two years ago when I started working at the daycare, worsening over time, often triggering Self-doubt and negative emotions when thinking about careers and job hunting.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to come to counseling because these thoughts cause me great distress and affect my academics and Work functioning; I am willing to try various approaches to feel better and gain clearer understanding of the future.
growth_experiences: started working at a daycare two years ago. Initially feeling conflicted and torn between 'accumulating Work experience' and 'seeking a major-related career path', gradually forming the belief that 'daycare Work will hinder major-related employment', worsening over time into uncertainty and Fear. Since then Self-doubt and negative emotions repeatedly appear when thinking about career prospects.
Seeing classmates obtain business-related internships or job opportunities while in school, feeling 'left behind', this social comparison triggered stronger anxiety and stress.

core_beliefs: if I do not have major-related experience now, I will be unable to enter major-related positions

special_situations.event: Seeing classmates obtain business-related internships or job opportunities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I have not gained major-related experience as promptly as classmates, it means I am behind or a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: rushing business-related internship applications, Reinforcing comparison with peers to push oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, I have been left behind.

special_situations.event: receiving internship rejection letters or long having no replies
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if rejected or receiving no replies, it proves I cannot enter this professional field
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Expands the interpretive force of negative evidence, reducing attention to other possibilities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: this proves I will never get into this industry.

special_situations.event: Looking back on two years working at the daycare
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if current Work is not directly major-related, this experience has no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets rigid timelines and rules, imposing strong time pressure on oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am wasting time, my degree will become utterly useless.

special_situations.event: thinking alone about careers and future job prospects
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I have no relevant experience now, I cannot enter major-related positions in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeks a sense of control by repeatedly rehearsing the worst outcomes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never find Work related to my major.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized professionally and gain a certain prospect, converting professional learning into achievement as soon as possible
core_conflict.fear: fear of failure, being left behind by peers, and years of academic investment becoming Meaninglessness
defense_goal: maintaining control with strict rules and timelines, reducing anxiety about uncertainty
Avoids feeling the pain of 'being left behind' through self-pressure and self-restraint

object_relations.object_representation: Peers/industry are like critical judges and gatekeepers

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing career timelines, rules, or seeing classmates get internships/jobs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: understanding 'not yet gaining relevant experience' as 'already failed/stereotyped', treating external standards as the sole judgment
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds mainly with rules and logic, emphasizing 'must/should', in a restrained tone touching little on the emotional level.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When comparing classmates' progress or ruminating alone after receiving a rejection letter
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: equating others' progress with one's own failure, producing self-blame and negation
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: reviewing one's inadequacies in a self-blaming tone, lowering self-worth expressions, dim tone, rarely using self-compassionate language.

manifestations: believing that failing to enter business positions soon will make one's degree 'become useless'
Viewing the time working at the nursery as a 'wasted opportunity'
outcomes: escalating Anxiety,Sleep and diet rhythm disturbance
academic Impaired concentration, tension in the partner relationship

manifestations: Restricts career path with 'must/should' rules, fears making the 'wrong choice'
Contracts multiple possibilities into a single path (must immediately obtain relevant experience)
outcomes: Rigid thinking, hard to experience flexibility and room for choice

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently talks about career timelines and experience requirements with 'must/should'
Treats industry and peer standards directly as one's only criterion for judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Reinforcing self-criticism and lowering self-worth in comparisons
Worries about 'falling behind'; maintains a sense of control through self-pressure

positive_force: Has a supportive partner and friend network, able to confide in difficult times
Proactiveness: has tried applying for business-related internships to challenge negative beliefs
clear professional background (business administration major), with a transferable ability foundation
negative_force: catastrophizing and predictive thinking (Fortune Telling), making worst-case assumptions about future employment
Overgeneralization and black-and-white thinking, negating the positive value of non-major-related Work
persistent rumination-induced Sleep and diet rhythm disturbance, further weakening functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent anxiety and rumination around career prospects (with Catastrophizing)
antecedent: Thinking about career and job prospects
Sees classmates obtaining business-related internships or jobs
receiving internship rejection letters or long having no replies
Realizes one has worked at the nursery for a long time
target_behavior.core_reason: predictive negative bias about future employment and rigid rules (like 'no relevant experience now means never getting in') maintaining Anxiety
target_behavior.function: seeking control by rehearsing worst outcomes and setting strict rules, temporarily escaping uncertainty-driven Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety worsened, declining academic focus, partner Relationship tension,Sleep and diet rhythms disrupted

antecedent: repeatedly worrying about careers and the future at night or when Being alone
Continuing to ruminate after social comparison or job-search setbacks during the day
target_behavior.core_reason: high-arousal anxiety and rumination disrupting physiological rhythms
target_behavior.function: distracting oneself by changing routines or diet, temporarily buffering Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Energy and focus decline, further affecting studies and emotional stability
